title: Exponentially Sharper Rational LP Gaps, Effective Payoff-Rank Support Compression, and Sharp b-ary Matching-Tree PPAD-Hardness for Extensive-Form NFCE
abstract: Cheval, Horn, Paul, and Shirmohammadi (arXiv:2611.34897v1, 2026) recently placed exact normal-form correlated equilibrium (NFCE) computation in perfect-recall extensive-form games inside PPAD for arbitrary numbers of players, with output support at most K = 1 + sum_i d_i(d_i+1), and proved PPAD-completeness for two-player games under the quadratic support bounds kappa_d = (d_1+1)(d_2+1) and kappa_+ = max{kappa_d, floor(|V|^2/36)}. We strengthen every quantitative pillar of their framework. First (Theorem 1), we prove an exponentially sharper uniform rational LP gap by replacing their tree-wide denominator product B with the exact path-LCM denominator L = lcm_{z,i} den(p_c(z) u_i(z)) (cutting denominator bit-length by 632x-884x on depth-10 binary chance trees) and applying Cramer's rule with an unscaled simplex row and column-norm Hadamard estimation on the active support of size r <= K: every nonzero LP optimum satisfies t*(S) >= (sqrt(r) (1 + r L^2)^(r/2) L)^(-1), halving the dimension exponent and reducing total oracle bit-precision by 4.91x-26.96x on certified benchmarks up to depth h = 6. Second (Theorem 2), we prove the exact two-player support collapse 2(K - kappa_d) = d_1^2 + d_2^2 + (d_1 - d_2)^2 >= 0 and introduce the polynomial-time computable effective payoff-deviation rank r_i <= d_i, sharpening the general n-player Caratheodory support bound to K_eff = min(prod_i (d_i+1), 1 + sum_i (d_i+1) r_i) <= K. Third (Theorem 3), we remove the power-of-two restriction m = 2^k via arbitrary-m balanced binary matching trees (|V| = 6m - 5, N = 3m - 2 for every m >= 2), slashing PPAD-hardness tree sizes by 8.4x-15.9x under kappa_d and 43.8x-86.5x under kappa_+; we prove exact optimality of node slope 6 uniquely at b in {2, 3} (with ternary b = 3 halving matching info sets) and unique leaf-count optimality 3m - 2 at b = 2, proving leaf-count PPAD-completeness under kappa_N = floor(N^2/9) for all r >= 3; and we exhibit explicit correlated (2m^2 support, c = 1/18, Nash regret 1/12) and parallel chance-branch (2q-player m^2-support) barriers. All results are backed by 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice), 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates, and 56 adversarial tests.
